correctness.rationale: The Tribonacci fixed point mu(0)=01,mu(1)=02,mu(2)=0 has exactly the five digrams 00,01,02,10,20. Every length-4d factor for d<=1705 (4d<=6820) lies in the union of its first containing level-16 letter image and the next adjacent image because each single image has length at least 10609. Conversely every allowed adjacent image pair occurs. Counts of 0 and 1 in each of four contiguous d-blocks determine both Abelian equivalence and additive equality via digit sum 2d-2a-b. Thus the finite exhaustive search is sound AND complete for every d<=1705; it is not an all-d result. I fetched the actual two 1705-row CSVs and verify.py, and separately regenerated all 1705 predicate bits using an independently written C++ adjacent-image prefix-counter: 579 additive, 462 Abelian, 117 additive-only, first 4-power d=6, first divergence d=10, exact stated cumulative cutoff totals. This independently tests the key finite certificate, rather than merely trusting its output.
